channel.title: Onchain Brief
channel.description: Crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, wallets, security incidents, regulation and new blockchain networks.

item.title: Is cBridge decentralized enough for your next transfer?
item.description: Is cBridge decentralized? Partly: SGN validators approve transfers, but a smaller set of contract role holders can pause or delay them. Here is what that means for your funds.

item.title: Keep bridged ETH or swap it for SUI after bridging
item.description: Keep bridged ETH on Sui or swap it for SUI? Hold ETH for Ethereum exposure, or swap some for SUI to cover gas and match your plans.

item.title: Fast Mode Shares More Data Before Ethereum Inclusion
item.description: Does fast mode on a private RPC reduce transaction privacy? Yes: it reaches more builders and TEE searchers before inclusion, while staying out of Ethereum’s public mempool.

item.title: One large buy vs several small buys for a new token: what to weigh
item.description: One large buy vs several small buys for a new token: one buy usually saves fees, while a small first buy and test sell can help check the exit.

item.title: How Long Do Cross-Chain Bridge Transfers Usually Take? By Route
item.description: Cross-chain bridge transfers usually take minutes to an hour; Bitcoin confirmations add time, while native optimistic rollup withdrawals to Ethereum take about seven days.

item.title: Repaying a DeFi loan starts with the borrowed token
item.description: How to repay a DeFi loan step by step: hold the borrowed token, approve a small buffer, then repay a set amount or max and confirm your balance falls.

item.title: CFTC staff say bitcoin and ether can count toward firm reserves
item.description: CFTC staff say derivatives firms may count bitcoin, ether and some stablecoins toward a year of operating resources, with discounts and cash limits.

item.title: Price impact vs slippage: how a swap’s cost changes
item.description: Price impact vs slippage: price impact sets the quoted cost; slippage is later pool movement your tolerance allows. See how each changes swap output.

item.title: How to withdraw Bitcoin to your own wallet and confirm it
item.description: To withdraw bitcoin from an exchange to your own wallet, create a wallet, back up its seed phrase, send BTC on Bitcoin, then track the txid to confirmation.

item.title: Slippage Tolerance: Set a Safe Minimum on a DEX
item.description: To choose slippage tolerance when a DEX shows high price impact, start with the smallest setting that works; the quote already includes price impact.

item.title: Why did sending to a new TRON address cost extra TRX? The one-time account fee
item.description: Sending TRX to a new TRON address can cost extra because the first transfer creates its on-chain account, adding a one-time fee and Bandwidth cost.

item.title: What Do You Need to Bridge Crypto From a Self-Custody Wallet?
item.description: What do you need to bridge crypto from a self-custody wallet? A supported route, the asset and gas on its source network, and a destination address.

item.title: MoonPay seeks US trust bank charter for stablecoin services
item.description: MoonPay has applied for a US trust bank charter to offer custody and stablecoin services under federal oversight, but the OCC has yet to decide.

item.title: Gnosis Bridge: Which transfer steps to double-check
item.description: Gnosis Bridge transfer refresher: check the route, source network and gas, then claim Ethereum withdrawals and confirm the destination balance on an explorer.

item.title: How to Swap Tokens on KyberSwap With MetaMask for One Trade
item.description: Learn how to swap tokens on KyberSwap with MetaMask: connect your wallet, approve an ERC-20 when asked, confirm the trade, and find the new token.

item.title: US gets court order over $1.2bn in stolen Binance crypto
item.description: The Justice Department won court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2bn tied to the Binance hack, part of $2.7bn frozen so far.

item.title: US gets court order over $1.2bn in stolen Binance crypto
item.description: The Justice Department says a court has authorized seizure or restraint of more than $1.2 billion from the Binance theft, as recovery efforts continue.

item.title: US wins court approval to seize $1.2B in Binance hack funds
item.description: The Justice Department says it won court approval to seize or restrain $1.2 billion tied to Binance’s $6.3 billion hack, as efforts to trace the funds continue.

item.title: How can I lower gas fees on my own Ethereum wallet?
item.description: How to reduce gas fees on your own Ethereum wallet: time the base fee, set a modest tip, use an L2 for routine activity and avoid failed transactions.
